direction: Keep the valid-time, retrieval-agnostic framing of D001/D002 and additionally fix the outcome hierarchy: version-level contamination and version confusion are primary; answer accuracy is a co-primary only on queries that pass an answer-differential screen (retrieving a non-gold version would change the reference answer); retrieval metrics and abstention are diagnostic. Report the answer-differential pass rate, and treat a low pass rate as an informative negative result about the practical significance of version confusion rather than a failure to measure.
hypothesis: On continuously amended regulatory text, valid-time (as-of) gating reduces version-level contamination and version confusion relative to semantic-only retrieval, elapsed-time decay and a hard as-of filter; the reduction in contamination translates into improved answer accuracy specifically on queries where retrieving a non-gold version would change the answer, and not on queries whose versions are answer-equivalent.
rationale: Point-in-time financial QA reports answer accuracy and temporal evidence leakage separately and adds a temporal-validity verifier, indicating accuracy alone does not capture temporal correctness; the regulatory retrieval benchmark reports only answer-quality metrics because it has no temporal dimension; SituatedQA's accuracy effects come from questions deliberately constructed so answers differ by temporal context; and the survey treats retrieval quality as the primary bottleneck with temporal mismatch as a failure mode that accuracy does not directly expose. This direction deserves investigation because it makes the evaluation falsifiable at two levels (version selection and end-task answer) and forces the study to report how often version confusion can actually change an answer, which is currently unknown and would determine whether the problem matters practically.
research_question: Does valid-time (as-of) gating applied post hoc to sparse, dense and hybrid retrievers reduce version-level temporal contamination and version confusion on continuously amended regulatory text relative to semantic-only retrieval, elapsed-time decay and a hard as-of filter, and does that reduction translate into improved answer accuracy specifically on queries where retrieving a non-gold version would change the reference answer?
